summary.abstract_hr: Marijan u podcastu Čušpajz govori o starijem bratu, dragovoljcu A satnije 105. bjelovarske brigade, koji je s prijateljem Stipom Gadžom poginuo 8. rujna (1991.) kod Pakraca, u Kusonjama. Opisuje njihov posljednji susret, telefonski razgovor noć prije akcije i šest mjeseci neizvjesnosti. Obitelj je brata tražila preko vlastitih kontakata, sve dok ekshumacija masovne grobnice u siječnju nije potvrdila njegovu smrt. Ispričao je i kako su obitelji tek nakon 33 godine, preko Ministarstva branitelja, dobile osobne stvari poginulih. Te su stvari pronađene nakon potresa u Zagrebu, odbačene u jednoj prostoriji na sudskoj medicini. Razgovor završava kritikom pravosuđa i najavom da će udruga ustrajati dok se ne izvrši pravda.
key_points: Marijanov brat bio je dio vremena u Njemačkoj, ali se vratio, prijavio u A satniju 105. bjelovarske brigade i otišao braniti Hrvatsku bez ikakvog kalkuliranja. Marijanu je žao što se pravi dragovoljci izjednačuju s onima koji su bili mobilizirani ili su sjedili u uredu.

Posljednji susret s bratom bio je kratak i u šali, oko 2. rujna, nakon pogibije Tihomira Vrdoljaka, prve žrtve s bjelovarskog područja. Večer prije akcije dečki su se iz Pakraca javili mami i šalili se s njom.

Nakon 8. rujna obitelj šest mjeseci nije znala sudbinu brata. Informacije su stizale neslužbenim kanalima, a obitelj se nadala da je brat zarobljen. Otac ga je pokušavao pronaći preko poznanika, pukovnika iz Titograda.
Smrt je potvrđena tek ekshumacijom masovne grobnice, koja je počela sredinom siječnja. Poginuli su pokopani na masovnom sprovodu 5. veljače 1992.

Prema Marijanu, ondje je bilo 18 bjelovarskih branitelja, uključujući neidentificiranog Tadiju Markića, te dva zagrebačka branitelja, Ivantić i Mato Čančar, ukupno 20. Time je ispravio broj od 17 koji se navodi u medijima.

Nakon 33 godine obitelji su preko Ministarstva branitelja dobile osobne stvari poginulih: satove, lančiće i privjeske A satnije. Stvari su slučajno pronađene nakon potresa u Zagrebu, odbačene u jednoj prostoriji Zavoda za sudsku medicinu. Marijan kaže da je zbog toga istodobno sretan i ljut.

Četvorica osuđenih odslužila su dio kazne i otišla u Srbiju, a protiv mnogih drugih povezanih osoba nije podignuta optužnica. Udruga, u kojoj sada ima i mlađih članova, najavljuje da će se pobrinuti da se pravda izvrši.
key_topics_en: return of personal belongings of the deceased
key_points_en: Marijan's brother was in Germany for part of the time, but he returned, signed up for Company A of the 105th Bjelovar Brigade, and went to defend Croatia without any calculating. Marijan regrets that true volunteers are equated with those who were mobilized or sat in an office.

The last meeting with his brother was brief and joking, around September 2, after the death of Tihomir Vrdoljak, the first victim from the Bjelovar area. The evening before the action, the guys called mom from Pakrac and joked with her.

After September 8, the family did not know the brother's fate for six months. Information arrived through unofficial channels, and the family hoped that the brother was captured. The father tried to find him through an acquaintance, a colonel from Titograd.
Death was confirmed only by the exhumation of the mass grave, which began in mid-January. The deceased were buried at a mass funeral on February 5, 1992.

According to Marijan, there were 18 Bjelovar veterans there, including the unidentified Tadija Markić, and two Zagreb veterans, Ivantić and Mato Čančar, a total of 20. With this, he corrected the number of 17 stated in the media.

After 33 years, the families received the personal belongings of the deceased through the Ministry of Veterans' Affairs: watches, chains, and Company A pendants. The belongings were accidentally found after the earthquake in Zagreb, discarded in a room of the Institute of Forensic Medicine. Marijan says that he is simultaneously happy and angry because of that.

The four convicted served part of their sentence and left for Serbia, and an indictment was not filed against many other connected persons. The association, which now also has younger members, announces that it will see to it that justice is served.
summary.abstract_en: In the podcast Čušpajz, Marijan speaks about his older brother, a volunteer of Company A of the 105th Bjelovar Brigade, who died with his friend Stipe Gadža on September 8 (1991) near Pakrac, in Kusonje. He describes their last meeting, a phone conversation the night before the action, and six months of uncertainty. The family searched for the brother through their own contacts, until the exhumation of a mass grave in January confirmed his death. He also recounted how the families only received the personal belongings of the deceased after 33 years, through the Ministry of Veterans' Affairs. Those belongings were found after the earthquake in Zagreb, discarded in a room at forensic medicine. The conversation ends with criticism of the judiciary and an announcement that the association will persevere until justice is served.
